Cross-level combat, senses, NPC travel, CE bridge (experimental), "Traveler" transit animations with a real pre-hop delay, blueprint art, wall risers, Perspective Shift + Toggleable Overlays support. Vertical links are now research-gated (4 projects) and the whole level plan can be switched off per colony. Workshop 3776015553, window 10 shipped. Window 11: §78, §79, §80 and §81 UNTESTED IN THE FIELD.
body:
**NOTE TO SELF:** running spec, not a changelog. §0 handover; §1-19 architecture; §20 compat; §21-29 bug records; §30 SUPERSEDED by §62; §31 publishing + GIT; §32-40 records; §41-44 combat/senses/travel/CE; §45-50 field-report fixes; §51 Celestial Lighting; §52 field-report round 2; §53 arrival/landing; §54 structure fit; §55 exit grid; §56 Geological Landforms; §57 stale decoration window; §58 relocated-structure fog; §59 forbid-aware islands; §60 area-linear vanilla systems; §61 camera-mod coexistence; §62 utility COLUMN rework + §62.N; §63 stairs permission; §64 cross-level shadow depth; §65 forbidden mirroring; §66 aim/wild-miss/aim-pie; §67 boulder extrusion; §68 KCSG/VFEM2; §69 stair temperature; §70 band flora legality + §70.B (OPEN); §71 Smooth Terrain (RESOLVED; report awaiting paste); §72 link gizmos; §73 transit animations (SUPERSEDED); §74 blueprint art; §75 wall risers; §76 Perspective Shift; §77 motion-study round 2 + §77b railing bug + §77c art defects; **§78 pre-hop delay + §78b-d the field fixes, RE-TEST PENDING**; **§79 Toggleable Overlays bridge, NEVER RUN**; **§80 research gating, NEVER RUN**; **§81 multiple-levels checkbox, NEVER RUN**. Keep every ⚠.

# As above, So below II (V2)

> **⚠⚠ V1 SOURCE IS NOT GONE. DATED SOURCE BACKUPS LIVE AT `D:\Rimworld\As above, So below\<yyyymmdd-hhmmss>\Source\`** (ten snapshots, newest `20260726-154207`). The old note "V1 survives only in git history pre-a50a744" was WRONG and cost a re-derivation. These are `Source/` only - no Defs, no Textures. **When a V2 feature has a V1 ancestor, READ THE V1 FILE FIRST.** Confirmed useful so far: `Source/Stairs/ClimbAnimation.cs` (§78d). Note the tool boundary: `read` refuses that path, `bash`/`grep`/`sed` reach it fine.

# 0. START HERE

**CURRENT PHASE: WINDOW 11. FOUR FEATURES COMPILE 0w/0e AND NONE HAS BEEN RUN: §78d, §79, §80, §81.** Three field rounds so far this window; each fixed real defects and found the next one.

**⚠ THE #297 QUESTION IS ANSWERED: THE HOLD DOES NOT DEADLOCK.** Runs 1-3 produced no stuck pawns and no bridge errors; every report has been cosmetic. The §78 mechanism (defer the MOVE, not the DECISION) is sound. If pawns ever stall at stairwells again the suspect list starts with `EntryCellFor`/the sweep's arrival clauses (§78c), NOT the hold.

Window 10 shipped §74/§75/§76 to Workshop 3776015553, pushed as **`afaf614`**. §78, §79, §80 and §81 are NOT committed.

**⚠ WORKSPACE DLL IS A DEBUG BUILD.** Rebuild Release before any publish.

**⚠ OWED, IN ORDER:** (1) **RE-TEST §78d.** (2) **FIELD-TEST §79** - needs Toggleable Overlays as a companionMod, and needs `quicktest=false` only if the TO settings window is part of the test. (3) **FIELD-TEST §80/§81** - §81 needs `quicktest=false` (it lives in the advanced-config dialog, which only exists on the new-colony path). (4) **WORKSHOP SMOKE TEST** from the WORKSHOP copy - never done for any window. (5) **FINAL riser art** (Gemini PAUSED r5; ⚠ REWRITE prompts to the REAL palette - NO copper: power=steel+blue+hazard, pipe=pale+red valve, climate=ice+louver+orange, data=black+purple+cyan). (6) **FOREIGN PRINT-PATH AUDIT** (ledger 4). (7) **§77c ART** - grand staircase east/west sprites unrotated; user's domain. (8) §62.N formal line. (9) Smooth Terrain upstream paste. (10) §70 Caverns verify. (11) Delete the retired ghost stubs. (12) **AnimationDef pipeline port** (§78d, OFFERED NOT ACCEPTED).

**⚠ SHIPPED KNOWINGLY UNVERIFIED (Workshop):** §62.N, §70 (w8); §62.M, §66c, §66e (w7). **⚠ PLACEHOLDER ART:** the 12 riser PNGs, by explicit user decision.

**⚠ USER WORKING RULES:** (1) NEVER source design ideas from other mods unless asked - scans COMPAT ONLY. **V1 is OUR OWN prior work and is exempt: porting from it is explicitly wanted.** (2) Building art = USER via Nano Banana kits. (3) About.xml description = USER's copy. (4) N mockups = N CHOICES.

**What this mod is.** Up to seven z-levels in ONE RimWorld `Map`, banded along +z. Priorities: visual clarity from above, performance, vanilla parity.

**⚠⚠ THE FORTY-EIGHT RULES:** 1. CLAMP AT SELECTION. 2. NEVER PATCH `TryRebuildDirtyRegionsAndRooms`. 3. REGION CONNECTIVITY IS MORE OPTIMISTIC THAN THE PATHFINDER: flood CELLS. 4. COUNT EMITTERS/POPULATIONS/ENGINE STACKS. 5 (§48): A `Touch` TARGET IS USUALLY UNWALKABLE. 6 (§49): A VANILLA HELPER CAN BE A NO-OP INSTEAD OF AN ERROR. 7 (§52): THE CARVE IS NOT THE LAST WORD. 8 (§52.6): A LOAD-TIME REPAIR PASS MUST NEVER RE-CREATE WHAT THE PLAYER DELIBERATELY REMOVED. 9 (§53): SOME MISPLACEMENTS ARE NOT VISIBLE IN THE CELL. 10 (§54): A STRUCTURE IS NOT A CELL. 11 (§55): A CELL-LEVEL VERDICT CANNOT AUTHORIZE A PAWN-LEVEL ACTION. 12 (§56a): A FOREIGN MOD'S MAP-SIZE SNAPSHOT IS AN INPUT YOU CAN CORRECT. 13 (§56g): NEVER COPY A GRID YOU DID NOT WATCH BEING WRITTEN. 14 (§56m): BEFORE RELOCATING DATA, ASK WHAT IS ALREADY AT THE DESTINATION. 15 (§57i): ASSERT ALWAYS, NARRATE ON REQUEST. 16 (§56o): COUNT THE FOREIGN MOD'S WRITE PATHS. 17 (§56q): A PASSING RUN THAT DID NOT REPRODUCE THE FAILURE IS NOT A FIX. 18 (§57a): NEVER EXONERATE A SUSPECT ON ONE CLEAN SAMPLE. 19 (§57f): `TicksGame` RESTARTS AT 0 EVERY NEW GAME. 20 (§57g): MOVING WORK EARLIER TURNS ON EVERY "IS THIS MAP READY" GATE. 21 (§58): THE PARALLEL GRIDS DO NOT TRAVEL WITH THE CONTENT. 22 (§59): A DERIVED GRID HAS NO PAWN IN IT. 23 (§60): AUDIT THE WEIGHTING, NOT THE SYMBOL. 24 (§61a): CLAMPING A VALUE WITHOUT CLAMPING ITS TARGET BUILDS AN OSCILLATOR. 25 (§61b): A POSTFIX ON `Update` IS AFTER THE OBJECT WAS ALREADY POSITIONED. 26 (§61f): EVERY READ OF THE MAP THE PLAYER CAN REACH MUST PASS THE RENDERER'S "IS IT DRAWN" GATE. 27 (§62c): PREFER SPAWN/DESPAWN OVER FLICK. 28 (§63a): A PERMANENT FICTION INSTALLED FOR ONE SUBSYSTEM IS READ AS FACT BY EVERY OTHER ONE. 29 (§0b): REPORT OUTCOMES, NOT INTENTIONS. 30 (§66d): A FELT DURATION IS A CHAIN, NOT A NUMBER. 31 (§66f): MAKE THE GUARD SAY WHICH CLAUSE DECLINED. 32 (§69a): TURNING OFF A TICK TURNS OFF EVERY SERVICE THAT RODE ON IT. 33 (§62k): A FILTER THAT CAN REJECT EVERYTHING MUST SAY SO. 34 (§62l): AN INVISIBLE THING IS ABSENT FROM EVERY SECTION LAYER. 35 (§62n): A CLONED FOREIGN DEF MADE VISIBLE IS IN NONE OF THE HOST'S OWN LOOKUPS. 36 (§70a): RUN VANILLA'S OWN LEGALITY PREDICATE. 37 (§71a): NAME THE ENFORCEMENT POINT BEFORE NAMING THE SYMPTOM. 38 (§73): WHEN A SPRITE MUST APPEAR AWAY FROM ITS THING'S POSITION, OWN THE DRAW. 39 (§76): WINNING THE LAST WRITE DOES NOT SETTLE A DISAGREEMENT ABOUT THE TARGET. 40 (§75.h): A TRIPWIRE THAT FIRES BEFORE THE OBSERVER ATTACHES IS NOT A TRIPWIRE. 41 (§77a): A STRUCT FIELD YOU NEVER SET IS A FEATURE YOU NEVER SHIPPED. 42 (§77b): THE DIRECTION A MOTION READS AS IS A PROPERTY OF THE THING, NOT OF THE ARRIVAL - and the far end is a DIFFERENT thing with its own axis. 43 (§78): **DEFER THE MOVE, NEVER THE DECISION.** 44 (§78b): AN OFFSET APPLIED WHOLE ON FRAME ONE IS A TELEPORT, AND EVERY `DrawPos`-DERIVED OVERLAY STAYS BEHIND. 45 (§78d): **A DIRECTION OF TRAVEL IS NOT A DIRECTION OF ELEVATION.** Sliding along the run axis and shrinking says "went away", not "went up" - a climb needs a SCREEN-SPACE vertical term that is independent of which way the run points. 46 (§78d): **NON-UNIFORM SCALE x ROTATION = SHEAR.** Ours is not the only matrix in the chain (parent body angle, per-node scales), so `sx != sz` while `rot != 0` skews the pawn into a parallelogram. Squash-and-stretch OR lean, never both. 47 (§79): **A FOREIGN MOD'S CACHED CURSOR CELL IS AN ASSUMPTION ABOUT COORDINATE SPACE.** When it gates N different draws on "is the mouse on this thing", SUBSTITUTE THE CELL AROUND OUR PASS instead of re-patching the N gates - one write fixes every gate it has, including ones it has not written yet. 48 (§81a): **A WRITE THAT IS READ BACK BY ITS OWN CALLER IS NOT A WRITE.** `Window.WindowOnGUI` does `windowRect = GUI.Window(ID, windowRect, ...)` - it passes the old rect in and assigns the result back AFTER the callback, so a windowRect set from inside `DoWindowContents` is clobbered in the same frame with no error. Find the assignment that follows your write before believing your write.

# 73. TRANSIT ANIMATIONS (V2 ROUND 1) — SUPERSEDED BY §78

Kept for the lesson. §73 shipped an INVERTED delay: instant carry, latency afterwards, as a ghost redrawn at the origin mouth while the real pawn stood at the destination. It existed because run #297 had deadlocked on a pre-hop hold. Its costs - a ghost draw pass, a hide pose, a suppressed name label, and a knowingly-shipped lie where the pawn was hittable at a destination it appeared not to be at - are all deleted by §78.

# 74. BLUEPRINT ART — SHIPPED w10, USER-VERIFIED

`ABBlueprintLook` retint; `Blueprint_ABBuild` stuff tint; `ABGhostGraphicForLinks` IsDoor bypass. Single knob, consumed in TWO places (blueprint `GraphicData.color` AND `Blueprint_ABBuild.DrawColor`, which must re-apply it over the stuff colour or a stuffed plan comes back opaque). **§74.b:** 0.70 read as ALREADY BUILT; now **0.42**. ⚠ NOT field-confirmed.

**⚠ §74.c (§79): THE KNOB IS NO LONGER A CONST.** `DefaultBlueprintAlpha` = 0.42 is the fallback; `BlueprintAlpha` is a mutable static driven by `ApplyAlpha(float)`, which also rewrites each retinted def's `GraphicData.color` and NULLS `GraphicData.cachedGraphic` (nothing public invalidates it, so a post-startup colour change would otherwise never reach the screen). Stuffed links need none of that - `Blueprint_ABBuild.DrawColor` reads the field per draw. Already-spawned blueprints keep the graphic they resolved on first draw, matching TO's own mid-game behaviour.

4 defs; a riser IS a `Building_ABColumn`; WallLamp attachment; no `holdsRoof`; cascade despawn. uiOrder: links 2060-2066, columns 2070-2073, risers 2080-2083. **§75.g `AB2: carrier probe`** - per-cell drawerType/IsCarrier/ShouldPrint census plus a live Harmony patch census. **Keep this tool.** **§75.h:** Dubwise layers derive from plain `SectionLayer`, declare NO `TakePrintFrom`, print from `Building_Pipe.PrintForGrid` - the old patch bound nothing for two windows. Now patched per host, deduped by MethodInfo, prefix INSPECTS the `SectionLayer` argument so unrecognised layers print rather than hide (rule 34). **⚠ §75.f IS PARTLY SUPERSEDED BY §80** - the architect ORDER note stands, the "no researchPrerequisites" note does not.

# 77. MOTION STUDY ROUND 2 — CLOSED. TRAVELER PICKED.

Five languages in `mockups/anim-A..E-*.html` over a shared kit: all four link types on the REAL art, 4-facing pawn, scrubbable timeline, PS avatar view, gold/red footprint edge markers, live C#-port panel. Machine-checked for NaN/range and railing crossings. **User picked C - Traveler at 0.30 playback** and asked for the delay to move BEFORE the hop. **D's structure-animation track (the building reacts) is the one unused idea worth revisiting** and is orthogonal to what shipped.

**⚠ §77a FACING (rule 41).** `PawnDrawParms.facing` is a writable `Rot4` on the struct our GetDrawParms postfix already takes by ref. **⚠ ALPHA: NO.** `tint` is writable but pawn materials are cutout; alpha needs `PawnRenderFlags.Invisible`, which routes through `InvisibilityMatPool.GetInvisibleMat` - a distortion shader with a hard-coded cyan multiply. Scale is the only vanish channel.

**§77b THE RAILING BUG, BOTH ENDS.** Decoded from the PNGs: every `*_south` sprite has its notch on its **NORTH** edge (`AB_StairsDown_south` north-edge coverage 42% vs 88/99/87). **Entry edge = `Opposite(Rotation)`, run direction = `Rotation.FacingCell`.** ⚠ **The counterpart shares this end's `Rotation` and that is load-bearing** (`GenAdj.AdjustForRotation` shifts even-sized footprints; `TryCellPairs` pairs cell i to cell i) - **DO NOT FLIP IT**.

**⚠ §77c ART DEFECTS - USER'S DOMAIN.** (a) `AB_GrandStairsDown/Up_east`/`_west` are the NORTH composition unrotated. (b) `AB_StairsDown_east/_west` differ in composition from north/south and sit 0.42 cells north. (c) `AB_StairsUp_east/_west` have no notch on any edge. (d) `AB_LadderUp_east` is a 0.14-cell sliver drawn 0.30 cells west. `ABStairAnim.ArtOffsets` transcribes these honestly.

# 78. PRE-HOP DELAY + THE V1 CLIMB GRAMMAR

**Structure.** `Carry` splits into `BeginCrossing` / `TickCrossings` / `CarryNow`. Both teleport sites (tick sweep AND `TryConsumeArrival`) route through it.

**⚠⚠ WHY THIS IS NOT RUN #297 (rule 43), AND THREE FIELD RUNS AGREE.** #297 held the pawn by REFUSING AN ARRIVAL, so `PatherArrived` never ran, the leg never completed, the job re-issued `StartPath`, `TrySegment` re-segmented forever. **The DECISION was deferred behind a cosmetic condition.** §78 defers only the POSITION WRITE: the record has already left `pending` and `everSegmented`, so there is no leg to re-segment. Held by **`StopDead()` + `StaggerFor`**, never by refusing an arrival - StopDead clears `moving` WITHOUT notifying the JobDriver, so the toil waits, no arrival fires at the stairwell, and `PatherTick` never re-tests `AtDestinationPosition`. On the arrival path, returning true is load-bearing and safe ONLY because StopDead already ran. Every exit teleports or abandons; anchor lost → `EndCurrentJob` (else it is `ABStuckWatchdog` episode B); job changed → cancel, no teleport; moved off the hold cell → fire early; `MaxHoldTicks` 300 backstops.

**§78b (field round 1: "teleports into the centre, nameplate wrong, facing wrong").** One root cause - the clip is authored about the LINK but nothing put the pawn AT the link. (1) **Travel, not teleport:** the absolute snap offset became `travelX/travelZ`, scaled by each pose's easing, so clips start at zero. (2) **Label follows the sprite:** postfix on `GenMapUI.LabelDrawPosFor(Thing, float)`; ⚠ delta computed in SCREEN space because the vanilla result is already projected AND y-flipped, so the y term subtracts. (3) **Facing from the actual vector**, not `Rotation.FacingCell`. (4) **`EntryCellFor`** rewrites the path destination to the link's entry side.

**§78c (field round 2: "still starts before they hit the stair texture").** The sweep carried any pawn within `ArriveRadius` = **3 cells**, so the clip began while the pawn was still walking. (1) `EntryCellFor` now returns the footprint cell just inside the notch - ⚠ tested with **`Walkable`, not `Standable`**, because a `Building_Door` is `PassThroughOnly` and `Standable` is false for every link cell. The approach is now real pathing at real walk speed. (2) The sweep waits for the pawn to be ON that cell. ⚠⚠ That is a NARROWER carry condition and narrowing it has jammed stairwells every previous time, so it is **delayed, never denied**: three triggers (on the cell / stopped short / `ApproachPatienceTicks` = 120 backstop) guarantee a crossing within two seconds.

**§78d (field round 3: "the animation isn't going up the stairs but in and down"). PORTED FROM V1** `Source/Stairs/ClimbAnimation.cs`. §78's Traveler grammar was slide-along-the-run + shrink-to-0.10 for BOTH directions - correct for a descent, meaningless for a climb (rule 45). V1 separates the terms, and its numbers are now ours verbatim:
- **SLIDE** toward the stairwell centre, eased, capped `SlideMax` 1.35 cells.
- **BOB** driven by TICKS not progress (period 12 stairs / 16 ladder, amp 0.05 / 0.08), so footfall rate is duration-independent.
- **VERT**, the actual fix: z −0.35 descending, +0.30 ascending. A screen-space rise/sink independent of which way the run points.
- **SCALE** ×0.72 descending, ×1.10 ascending - modest, and **uniform** (rule 46; the old non-uniform sx/sz with a lean was shearing the sprite into a parallelogram).
- **LEAN** `Sin(t*PI/24)*3°`, stairs only; ladders climb square-on, elevator passengers do not sway.
- **EMERGE** 22 ticks, ease-out `(1-p)²`, vertical INVERTED against the climb (down arrives from above: raised and ×1.12 settling; up arrives from below: sunken and ×0.82 growing).
- **Durations** now V1's: climb 90 ticks (ladder 110, elevator 90 + 16/level capped 130), emerge 22.

**⚠ OFFERED, NOT ACCEPTED: THE PIPELINE ITSELF.** V1 drove this through the native `AnimationDef` + `BaseAnimationWorker` API (`SetAnimation`, `OffsetAtTick`/`AngleAtTick`/`ScaleAtTick`) rather than a `GetDrawParms` matrix. That is strictly better for compat - it composes with Yayo's, Melee Animation and facial mods, and V1 explicitly checked `renderer.CurAnimation` to **never stomp a foreign animation**. Only the grammar was ported; the pipeline swap is ledger 13.

**⚠ RETIRED STUBS.** `IsGhosting` returns constant false and `DrawGhosts` is a no-op, documented, because they have live call sites in `ABBelowDynamicDraw`. Delete once §78 is proven.

# 79. TOGGLEABLE OVERLAYS — `Source/Compat/ToggleableOverlaysCompat.cs`, COMPILES, NEVER RUN

Bridge to `Owlchemist.ToggleableOverlays` (the "Continued" reupload keeps that packageId; ws 3261316725). House rules as always: reflection-only, no foreign type in any signature, no patch attribute on the bridge class, inert and silent when absent. Reads go through Harmony `FieldRef` delegates, NOT `FieldInfo.GetValue`, because two of them sit on the per-frame overlay path that was once profiled at 1.41 ms - boxing an int per thing per frame there is not acceptable. **Bound shape:** `ToggleableOverlaysUtility.mousePositionX/mousePositionZ/mousePosition/quickView`; `ModSettings_ToggleableOverlays.hideForbidden/hideForbiddenBuildings/optimizedLister/zoomFilter/blueprintTransparency`; `Mod_ToggleableOverlays.WriteSettings`. The mouse trio is load-bearing (missing ⇒ one `WarningOnce`, bridge off); every other member degrades to "behave as if that toggle were off".

**⚠ 79.1 THE COORDINATE-SPACE BUG, AND IT IS THE WHOLE REASON THIS EXISTS (rule 47).** TO's premise is "the overlay only appears for the thing under the cursor", and every one of its ~10 gates is literally `thing.positionInt.x == mousePositionX && thing.positionInt.z == mousePositionZ` against a cell derived in `Patch_Game_UpdatePlay` from a raw `ScreenPointToRay` - i.e. **the VIEW band's cell**. A below-band thing lives at `z - drop`, so its position can NEVER equal that, and no below overlay is reachable by hover. With TO's shipped defaults (`hideItems`, `hideStorageBuilding`, `hideBedAssignment`, `hideFuelWarnings` all ON) that silently deletes stack counts, storage labels, bed/throne names and fuel warnings from every level below the viewed one, permanently. **Fix = ONE substitution, not ten patches:** `PushBelowMouse` saves their three fields and points them at the cell the hovered column actually shows (same `ABBands.TryResolveVisibleBelow` the renderer and label placer use), `PopMouse` restores in a `finally`. Every TO gate then answers correctly without knowing bands exist - including gates they have not written yet. ⚠ The cursor cell is read FROM THEIR OWN FIELDS, not recomputed from `UI.MouseCell` (they truncate a ray origin, we would floor a projected point; the two disagree off-map). ⚠ Off-map / opaque column / `drop == 0` parks the mouse at `IntVec3.Invalid` rather than leaving the view-band value - harmless either way (bands PARTITION z, so a below thing's z can never equal a view-band z, which is exactly why the bug is "never reveals" and never "reveals the wrong thing") but rule 28 says do not leave a fiction lying around. ⚠ The `finally` is non-negotiable: a mouse left parked on a below cell hides every overlay on the CURRENT level until the cursor moves.

**79.2 FORBIDDEN MARKERS.** `Patch_OverlayDrawer_ABBelowForbidden` paints the X with a bare `Graphics.DrawMesh` and never enters `OverlayDrawer.RenderForbiddenOverlay`, where TO's transpiler lives - so with "hide forbidden" on, the current level's X's vanished and the level below's stayed lit. `AllowForbiddenBelow` re-implements their `CheckRenderForbiddenOverlay` + `RenderForbiddenBigOverlay` against the substituted mouse: `quickView` short-circuits true; neither setting on ⇒ true; **their zoom gate (`CurrentZoom > Middle` ⇒ false) applies to EVERY category once either setting is on**, because it is injected at the top of the method; `Item` ⇒ cell-to-cell compare (their call passes `sizeOne: true`); `Building`/`Ethereal` ⇒ `GenAdj.IsInside` footprint test. Settings are read LIVE, which is correct even though their patches are `Prepare()`-gated: their `WriteSettings` does `UnpatchAll` + `PatchAll` on every write, so their own behaviour tracks live values too.

**79.3 ZOOM CULLING — THEIR SLIDER WINS (user decision).** Their `ThingOverlays` transpiler swaps the lister group from `HasGUIOverlay` (38) to `Pawn` (12) at any zoom above `Closest` when `optimizedLister && zoomFilter`. Our below pass walked `HasGUIOverlay` unconditionally, so zoomed out the level below showed labels the current level had already culled. `BelowOverlayGroup` mirrors their choice and falls back to `HasGUIOverlay` whenever TO is absent or a setting failed to bind.

**79.4 BLUEPRINT ALPHA — THEIR SLIDER WINS (user decision), rule 39.** `Mod_ToggleableOverlays.WriteSettings` walks every blueprint ThingDef and writes `graphic.color.a = blueprintTransparency`, and it runs from their `[StaticConstructorOnStartup]` AND again every time their settings window closes. Racing them is unwinnable (load order decides the startup winner; the settings window re-stomps forever), so we ADOPT: a parameterless postfix on that same method calls `ABBlueprintLook.ApplyAlpha(Clamp01(theirs))`. Result is load-order independent and survives every settings write. **⚠ KNOWN AND ACCEPTED CONSEQUENCE: their slider DEFAULTS TO 1.0**, which is a no-op in their world but for us means fully opaque plans - the §74.b "reads as already built" look - for any TO user who never opens TO's settings. Reversing it is one line in `SyncBlueprintAlpha` (`Mathf.Min(theirs, DefaultBlueprintAlpha)`). **This is the first thing to look at in a §79 field test.**

**79.5 NOT BRIDGED, DELIBERATELY.** Their `Patch_MoteProgressBar` / `Patch_DrawFillableBar` gate world-space gauges on the same cursor cell; we do not redraw below-band fillable bars at all, so there is nothing to fix today. Ledger 14.

# 80. RESEARCH GATING FOR THE VERTICAL LINKS — `Defs/V2/AB2_Research.xml`, NEVER RUN

Four free-standing `ResearchProjectDef`s, no prerequisites of their own, by explicit user decision. Every AB2 buildable is now behind exactly one of them; nothing else about the buildings changed.

| project | label | cost | tech | tags | gates |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AB2_Stairs` | stairs | 400 | Neolithic | ClassicStart | stairs up/down **and both grand staircases** |
| `AB2_Ladders` | ladders | 400 | Neolithic | ClassicStart | ladder up/down |
| `AB2_TransferColumns` | transfer columns | 1200 | Industrial | — | the 4 utility columns **and the 4 wall risers** |
| `AB2_ElevatorTech` | elevator | 1600 | Industrial | — | the elevator |

**80.1 WHERE THE PREREQUISITE IS STATED.** Per-def on `AB2_StairsDown`/`AB2_StairsUp` (they inherit `AB2_LinkBase`, which also parents the ladders and the elevator - a base-level statement would gate all seven on one project), and on the abstract bases `AB2_GrandBase`, `AB2_LadderBase`, `AB_ColumnBase`, `AB_WallRiserBase`.

**⚠ 80.2 THE PROJECT IS `AB2_ElevatorTech`, NOT `AB2_Elevator`.** defNames are unique per DefType only, so a ResearchProjectDef named `AB2_Elevator` would legally coexist with the ThingDef of that name and make every log line, xpath and search about "AB2_Elevator" ambiguous. The label the player sees is still "elevator".

**⚠ 80.3 THIS PARTLY REVERSES §75.f, AND THE OLD REASONING IS PRESERVED, NOT DISCARDED.** §75.f removed researchPrerequisites from the columns because Electricity + Machining left a fresh banded colony unable to join its levels' utilities until mid game. `AB2_TransferColumns` has NO prerequisites, so that concern is answered by construction: the only thing between a new colony and its columns is bench time, available from turn one. The per-network connect toggles still consult each host mod's own research (`Building_ABColumn.GetGizmos` → `AB2_ColumnNeedsResearch`), so an unresearched foreign network still cannot be carried with this finished. §75.f's ARCHITECT ORDER note (uiOrder 2060-2083) is untouched and still authoritative.

**⚠ 80.4 TRIBAL STARTS BEGIN WITH NO WAY DOWN.** `FactionDef PlayerColony` lists ClassicStart in `startingResearchTags`, so standard starts know stairs and ladders immediately. `PlayerTribe` does not, so a tribal colony must spend 400 before it can leave the level it was given - deliberate, and reversible with one `<li>TribalStart</li>`. **This is the thing to actually watch in a field test.**

**⚠ 80.5 ROW 6.40 IS AN EMPTY ROW TODAY.** The tallest vanilla project across Core + all DLCs sits at `researchViewY` 5.70, so 6.40 is ours alone; X 0/1 sit under the neolithic column and 6/7 under the industrial block. Recheck if a DLC ever extends the tree downward. No custom `ResearchTabDef` and no `iconPath`.

# 81. "ENABLE MULTIPLE LEVELS" CHECKBOX — COMPILES, NEVER RUN

A checkbox on the **Levels** heading row of the advanced-config dialog (`Dialog_AdvancedGameConfig`), collapsing the whole bottom strip, backed by a new scribed setting `ABSettings.multiLevel` (default true).

**81.1 IT SUSPENDS THE PLAN, IT DOES NOT ERASE IT (and that is why it is not just "set both spinners to 0").** `upperLevels`/`lowerLevels` keep whatever the player chose; `ABMapSizeLimit.MultiLevel` gates only the EFFECTIVE `UpperLevels`/`LowerLevels`, which read 0 while it is off. `BandCount` collapses to 1 and `Patch_MapGenerator_GenerateMap` takes its pre-existing "single level - generate an ordinary map" branch, so **no new generation path was added**. Re-ticking restores the plan intact.

**81.2 IT ALSO HANDS BACK THE MAP-SIZE COLUMN.** `ABMapSizeLimit.Active` now includes `MultiLevel`. Unticked ⇒ `Fits` is unconditional, `Clamp` is the identity, `BeginChooser` returns before it locks or relabels anything, and the every-frame `GameInitData.mapSize` snap stops - vanilla's own size list is live again. On the tick-OFF transition `mapSize` is forced to **250**, because our tiers (126/190/254) are not in vanilla's list and the radio column would otherwise come back with nothing selected. Tick-ON needs no counterpart: `Active` is live, so the existing snap clamps 250 onto the ladder on the same frame. `AB_MapSizeLockedTip` now opens "Locked by the multiple levels setting:" instead of naming the mod.

**⚠ 81.3 THE WINDOW RESIZE, WHICH IS THE ONLY HARD PART (rule 48).** `Window.WindowOnGUI` ends with `windowRect = GUI.Window(ID, windowRect, callback, ...)` - it passes the OLD rect in and assigns Unity's return value back AFTER the callback returns. `DoWindowContents` runs inside that callback, so a `windowRect` written from the chooser is overwritten in the same frame, silently, with no error. The rect is therefore parked in a static and applied by `Patch_Window_ABResizeAfterDraw`, a postfix on the base `Window.WindowOnGUI` - the one point past that assignment. It is on every window's draw path in the game, so its first line is a `ReferenceEquals` bail with nothing allocated above it, and it is armed only by a checkbox click. (`resizeLater`/`resizeLaterRect` would also work but is gated on `resizeable`, which would give the dialog a user-draggable resize handle.)

**⚠ 81.4 LAY OUT AGAINST THE HEIGHT YOU WERE GRANTED, NOT THE HEIGHT YOU WANT.** `InitialSize` is consulted exactly once, by `Window.SetInitialSizeAndPosition`, so the checkbox cannot change the window height by itself. The strip is anchored from `ABMapSizeLimit.GrantedStripHeight` (set in the `InitialSize` postfix, updated when a resize lands); `WantedStripHeight` is 240 expanded / 44 collapsed and window height is `vanilla + granted + StripPadding(48)` - the old flat `+288` was exactly `240 + 48`. Ticking ON inside a window still sized for 44 draws the collapsed row for **one frame** and skips the section rather than punching it through vanilla's columns.

**81.5 FIELD-TEST CHECKLIST (needs `quicktest=false` - the dialog only exists on the new-colony path).** Untick: bottom section vanishes, window shrinks and re-centres, vanilla Small/Medium/Large unlock and are clickable, 250 is selected. Re-tick: section returns, window grows, vanilla sizes lock again with the new tooltip wording, a tier is selected. Close and reopen the dialog in each state: it should open at the right height already. Then actually generate in the OFF state and confirm an ordinary single-level map at a vanilla size, and in the ON state that nothing changed.
